maya: Heads up — bringing up hf://open-llm/zephyr-7b into Redwood staging. Our eval harness shows a consistent drop on token-level metrics vs the HF baseline (same weights). Suspect tokenizer conversion issue (normalization / pretokenization). Anyone seen NFC/NFD + byte-fallback combos cause this?

dylan: yep. If the HF tokenizer was trained with NFD but the conversion normalizes to NFC you get different byte fallback for accented chars. Quick reproducer: `tokenizer.encode('café')` vs `tokenizer.encode('cafe\u0301')` returns different ids on our converted tokenizer.

katie: can you paste exact outputs? also which `from_pretrained` flags used during conversion? fast vs slow matters.

dylan: sure — HF (original) -> `use_fast=True`
- `tokenizer_hf.encode('café') -> [124, 56, 999]`
- `tokenizer_hf.encode('cafe\u0301') -> [124, 56, 999]`
Converted -> `use_fast=False`
- `converted.encode('café') -> [124, 56, 999]`
- `converted.encode('cafe\u0301') -> [124, 56, 1023]`
So NFD form ends up using byte-fallback path on the converted tokenizer.

samir: that byte-fallback id difference will change attention pattern and likely hurt eval. Did the conversion script drop the normalizer section from `tokenizer.json`? I remember we had a bug that stripped `normalizer` and `pre_tokenizer` when mapping HF files to Redwood bundle.

maya: good call. I grepped the conversion log — `convert-bot` printed a warning: `missing normalizer -> defaulting to none`. attach: convert-bot: "Dropped normalizer: nfkc(\"\" -> none)"

convert-bot: noticed mapping mismatch: source tokenizer has `normalizer` : {"type":"Sequence","normalizers":[{"type":"NFD"}]}, target bundle left normalizer empty. Conversion rule `keep_normalizer` defaulted false.

katie: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) patch conversion to preserve `normalizer` (NFD/NFC) and `pre_tokenizer`; 2) add a normalization unit test (round-trip on accented chars + whitespace); 3) run staging eval with `enable_prefix_space` toggle — chat-style models often need `add_prefix_space=true`.

dylan: also check `split_on_whitespace` vs byte fallback: we saw tokens merge when leading space missing. Example: `tokenizer.encode(' hello')` vs `'hello'` — chat templates that expect a leading space can change token distribution. Our conversion removed `add_prefix_space` for `GPT-Chat` style wrappers.

maya: here's a small patch I tested locally (pseudo):
```
# conversion step
if 'normalizer' in hf_tokenizer_json:
    rd_tokenizer['normalizer'] = hf_tokenizer_json['normalizer']
if hf_tokenizer_json.get('add_prefix_space'):
    rd_tokenizer['pre_tokenizer']['add_prefix_space'] = True
```
fixed unit test case: `'cafe\u0301'` now encodes identical to `'café'` and staging eval north of baseline by +0.6% token-f1.

samir: nice. Can we add a small fuzz test: random unicode combining chars + whitespace permutations to the onboarding harness? That would catch regressions when we change converter logic.

katie: I'll add a test and flag new model onboarding to fail if any token diff occurs for NFKC/NFKD variations of the 1k most common glyphs. Also adding conversion metadata in the model bundle: `tokenizer_normalizer_preserved: true/false`.

maya: action items: katie -> add tests + gating (ETA tomorrow), dylan -> PR to preserve normalizer and pre_tokenizer in converter, samir -> run quick staging eval after PR merge. I'll include the failing HF vs converted token diffs in the model onboarding ticket. Thanks team :thumbsup:

convert-bot: conversion job 1779004321 updated: rule `keep_normalizer` toggled on for future runs.
